easy.def: Land with water all around it.
examples: We took a boat to the island.
The island has a sandy beach.
Birds live on the small island.

more.def: A piece of land that is completely surrounded by water.
examples: Hawaii is made up of many islands in the Pacific Ocean.
The only way to reach the island is by ferry.
They built a hut on the island in the middle of the lake.

easy.def: A person who lives on an island.
examples: The islander fished.
An islander lives by the sea.
The islanders sailed.

more.def: A person who lives on an island.
examples: The islander fished from a small boat.
The islanders greeted the ferry each day.
Many islanders make a living from the sea.
We sailed to the isle.
The isle has a lighthouse.
Birds live on the isle.

more.def: A small island, often used in stories and place names.
examples: A tiny isle with palm trees lay just off the coast.
The ferry carried us to the quiet isle.
Pirates in the story hid treasure on a lonely isle.
A bird sat on the islet.
The islet is tiny.
We saw an islet.
Seagulls nested on the rocky islet.
We rowed out to a tiny islet in the lake.
A single palm tree grew on the islet.
The nurse will isolate the sick child.
Snow isolated the cabin.
We isolate the sick plant.

more.def: To keep a person, animal or thing apart from others, or to separate one part from the rest.
examples: A sick student stays home to isolate himself from the class until he is better.
Heavy snow isolated the village from the rest of the world for days.
The scientist isolated one tiny seed from the pile to study it.

easy.def: Being all alone and far from others.
examples: The island is in isolation.
He felt isolation in the new town.
The hermit lived in isolation.

more.def: The state of being alone or far away from other people or places.
examples: The little cabin sits in isolation, miles from the nearest town.
The explorers lived in isolation on the ice for six months.
Penguins in the far south live in isolation from many other animals.

easy.def: A problem that people talk about.
examples: Litter is an issue.
The issue is noise.
Let us talk about the issue.

more.def: A subject or problem that people think and talk about.
examples: Litter in the park is an important issue.
The class talked about the issue of recycling.
Noise is an issue in the hallway.
This issue has a puzzle.
I read the new issue.
The May issue came today.

more.def: One edition of a magazine or newspaper that comes out at a certain time.
examples: The December issue has a story about owls.
She saved every issue of the magazine.
This week's issue is on the table.

easy.def: A narrow strip of land with water on both sides.
examples: An isthmus is a strip of land.
The isthmus connects two lands.
We crossed the isthmus.

more.def: A narrow strip of land that joins two larger pieces of land and has water on both sides.
examples: The isthmus joins the two continents.
Panama is on an isthmus.
We walked across the isthmus between the two bays.
